rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent bent-and-cantilevered mass in all four views, so it clears the multi-view coherence test. The dominant gesture is legible and the silhouette has enough continuity to avoid a purely box-like read. However, the public-ground response to the verified access edge is weak: the mass is largely sealed, with only a limited notch/cut that does not produce a strong court, undercut, or entry seam. Parcel response is acceptable because the form sits coherently within the boundary and does not visibly collide across views. Programmatically, the mass can plausibly support neighborhood living/mixed-use as a compact capacity-aware bar, but it under-expresses the active threshold and public void called for in the brief. The references support a coherent single-object mass with controlled deformation; the candidate aligns more with the mixed-use/tower-derived precedent language than the café reference, though all remain only partially transferable.
